subject: English Literature
content: Modern texts and poetry: Students must answer one question from Section A (Modern prose or drama), one question from Section B (Poetry from the AQA Anthology), and both questions in Section C (Unseen poetry).

subject: English Literature
content: Section A: Modern prose or drama. Students study one text from the following list and answer one question on it: JB Priestley's *An Inspector Calls*, Willy Russell's *Blood Brothers*, Chinonyerem Odimba's *Princess & The Hustler*, Dennis Kelly's *DNA*, Winsome Pinnock's *Leave Taking*, Shelagh Delaney's *A Taste of Honey*, William Golding's *Lord of the Flies*, AQA Anthology *Telling Tales*, George Orwell's *Animal Farm*, Kit de Waal's *My Name Is Leon*, Meera Syal's *Anita and Me*, Stephen Kelman's *Pigeon English*.

subject: English Literature
content: JB Priestley: *An Inspector Calls*. Questions focus on: (1) How Priestley presents Gerald and Sheila’s changing relationship; (2) How Priestley presents ideas about power.

subject: English Literature
content: Willy Russell: *Blood Brothers*. Questions focus on: (1) How Russell presents the changes in Mickey and Edward’s relationship; (2) How Russell presents the effects of social class.

subject: English Literature
content: Chinonyerem Odimba: *Princess & The Hustler*. Questions focus on: (1) How Odimba presents the relationship between Mavis and Princess; (2) How Odimba presents Princess’s dreams as important to her.

subject: English Literature
content: Dennis Kelly: *DNA*. Questions focus on: (1) How Kelly uses the character of Leah to explore ideas about human nature; (2) How Kelly uses the character of Adam to explore ideas about bullying.

subject: English Literature
content: Winsome Pinnock: *Leave Taking*. Questions focus on: (1) How Pinnock presents difficult relationships between older and younger characters; (2) How far Pinnock presents the character of Enid as a strong mother.

subject: English Literature
content: Shelagh Delaney: *A Taste of Honey*. Questions focus on: (1) How far Delaney presents Peter as a selfish and unpleasant character; (2) How Delaney presents characters in conflict with each other.

subject: English Literature
content: William Golding: *Lord of the Flies*. Questions focus on: (1) How Golding presents the changing relationship between Ralph and Jack; (2) How far Golding uses the character of Simon to explore ideas about goodness.

subject: English Literature
content: AQA Anthology: *Telling Tales*. Questions focus on: (1) How writers present characters dealing with loss in ‘Odour of Chrysanthemums’ and one other story; (2) How writers present conflict between generations in ‘Korea’ and one other story.

subject: English Literature
content: George Orwell: *Animal Farm*. Questions focus on: (1) How far Orwell suggests that no society can ever be truly equal; (2) How far Orwell presents Napoleon as responsible for the failure of the revolution.

subject: English Literature
content: Kit de Waal: *My Name Is Leon*. Questions focus on: (1) How de Waal presents the importance of Maureen in Leon’s life; (2) How de Waal explores ideas about loyalty.

subject: English Literature
content: Meera Syal: *Anita and Me*. Questions focus on: (1) How far Syal presents Anita as a powerful character; (2) How Syal uses the setting of Tollington to explore ideas about how society is changing.

subject: English Literature
content: Stephen Kelman: *Pigeon English*. Questions focus on: (1) How Kelman presents the effects of violence on Harrison and his community; (2) How far Kelman presents Miquita as a frightening and threatening character.

subject: English Literature
content: Section B: Poetry from the AQA Anthology *Poems Past and Present*. Students answer one question from one of the following clusters: Love and relationships, Power and conflict, Worlds and lives.

subject: English Literature
content: Love and relationships cluster. Compare how poets present feelings about growing up in ‘Follower’ (Seamus Heaney) and one other poem from the cluster.

subject: English Literature
content: Power and conflict cluster. Compare how poets present ideas about conflict in ‘Exposure’ (Wilfred Owen) and one other poem from the cluster.

subject: English Literature
content: Worlds and lives cluster. Compare how poets present the ways places affect people’s lives in ‘In a London Drawingroom’ (George Eliot) and one other poem from the cluster.

subject: English Literature
content: Section C: Unseen poetry. Students answer both questions: (1) How the poet presents feelings about home and family in an unseen poem; (2) Compare the methods poets use to present feelings about home and family in two unseen poems.

subject: English Literature
content: AO4 assessment: Use a range of vocabulary and sentence structures for clarity, purpose, and effect, with accurate spelling and punctuation. Assessed in Section A (4 marks).
